AI is optional.
Control is mandatory.

Greentic digital workers run whole processes end to end against the systems you already use, then sign an audit line for every step they took.

Not a chatbot, and not an agent that improvises. Workflows execute exactly as defined, so the thousandth run behaves like the first.

02 / THE CHOICEWhy this and not an agent

Three ways to put AI to work. One is safe to run the business on.

Agent frameworks are genuinely good at assistance. Copilots are good inside the productivity suite. Neither was built to own a process that settles money, grants access, or promises a customer a delivery date.

Agent frameworks

LangChain, CrewAI and similar
  • Flexible but unpredictable
  • Hard to control
  • Hard to audit
  • Risky in production
  • Good for assistance only

Enterprise copilots

Microsoft Copilot Studio and similar
  • Limited integration depth
  • Limited control over execution
  • Not for core business automation

Greentic digital workers

Deterministic execution, AI where it helps
  • Predictable execution
  • Full control and audit
  • Production ready
  • Fast, low cost workflows
  • Built for core processes
Control

Governance built in

Policy enforcement, routing rules, access control and business logic constraints, so the right actions happen every time.

Observability

Every run is readable

Full visibility into every workflow execution. Trace, debug and monitor in real time rather than guessing after the fact.

Integration

It acts, not just answers

MCP based integrations, APIs, OpenAPI services, CRM, ERP and internal systems, secured with OAuth on every connection.

03 / ANATOMYWhat you actually get

A worker is assembled, not prompted into existence

Each layer is a real, inspectable thing you own. That is what makes a run repeatable, and what lets someone change one step without rewriting the worker.

01

Component

One capability. A lookup, a policy check, an API call, a message out.

02

Flow

Components joined into a sequence, with the decisions and branches written down.

03

Application pack

Flows bundled for a domain, plus extension packs for analytics, languages and control.

04

Digital worker

The deployed bundle. It runs on its own and handles an entire domain of work.

Change it yourself

Adjust by describing the change

Describe what should happen differently in plain language and the flow is updated. The result is still a defined workflow you can read, not a prompt that behaves differently each time.

Global from day one

Multilingual, not translated later

Workers take a request in any language and answer in the same one, which is why the customer self-service worker can cover every market at once.

04 / THE HANDOVERWhat the shift leaves behind

Every run signs its own record

This is the difference between automation you hope worked and automation you can answer for. When someone asks why an account was credited or who approved an access change, the answer is a document, not an investigation.

Trace

Replay any run

Step through what happened in the order it happened, including the branches that were not taken.

Answer

Attribute every decision

Each step names the rule that allowed it and the person who approved it, where a person was involved.

Export

Hand it to whoever asks

The record leaves the platform in a form an auditor, a regulator or a customer can actually read.

06 / THE PATHProblem to production

From a described problem to a governed production worker

Greentic calls this the 3P method. The point of it is that you see something working before you commit to anything.

STEP 01

Problem

Explain what is slow, manual or broken today, in plain language. No process maps or technical specification needed to start.

STEP 02

Working demo

Greentic turns that description into a working AI powered process you can experience, refine and demonstrate, often inside the first meeting. It runs real journeys, integrations, approvals and human decisions.

STEP 03

Production

Once the journey is proven, Greentic and its forward deployment engineering partners take it from demo to governed production in weeks, not months or years.

Before you ask

What if our process is not one of the five?

The five on the roster are the ones already built. The method starts from your description, not from a catalogue, so an unlisted process is the normal case rather than the exception.

Do we have to replace anything we already run?

No. Workers connect to the systems you have through MCP, APIs and OpenAPI services, secured with OAuth. The worker is the layer that acts across them.

What happens when a worker gets something wrong?

The run stops at the step that failed and the record shows which rule refused it. Steps that need judgement are configured to wait for a person rather than guess.

Who owns the workflows we build?

The platform is open source, and the flows and packs are inspectable artifacts rather than a hosted black box.

How much does it cost?

Greentic does not publish pricing, and this concept does not invent any. Cost is scoped against the process and the systems involved, in the first conversation.

Not ready to talk? The platform is open source, so you can read how a worker is assembled, browse the roster, or come in through a delivery partner instead.
